examples: Taking into consideration customer feedback, engineers redesigned the mobile application user interface.

definitions: to a moderate extent or degree; somewhat or approximately in informal context
examples: He felt sort of disappointed when the concert was postponed until next month.

definitions: to some extent or degree; rather or somewhat in informal speech
examples: The instructions were kind of confusing, so we asked for further clarification.

definitions: approximately, nearly, or for the most part; with minimal variation or difference
examples: The renovations are more or less complete, except for painting the front door.

definitions: plus or minus a specified amount; approximately or roughly in estimation
examples: The drive to the airport takes about two hours, give or take twenty minutes.

definitions: used to indicate that an estimate, figure, or statement is approximate
examples: Roughly speaking, half of the population participated in national voting elections yesterday.

definitions: used to introduce a figure of speech or unusual expression politely
examples: The company experienced a digital rebirth, if you will, after rebranding completely.

definitions: used to highlight that a word or phrase is being used metaphorically
examples: We are sailing in uncharted waters, so to speak, with this new technology.

definitions: used to qualify a statement that might seem unusual, metaphorical, or non-literal
examples: He was the captain of our team, as it were, guiding our efforts.

definitions: used in casual speech to confirm that the listener understands implied meaning
examples: The atmosphere was tense, if you know what I mean, during negotiations.

definitions: used after explaining an idea to check whether the listener has understood
examples: We need to streamline operations to save costs, if that makes sense.

definitions: used when offering a tentative, informal summary or interpretation of a situation
examples: I guess you could say our expansion strategy exceeded all our initial expectations.

word: when all is said and done
definitions: when everything has been considered, concluded, or brought to a close
examples: When all is said and done, customer satisfaction remains our highest priority.
synonyms: at the end of the day

definitions: used to state that a lengthy explanation is being summarized briefly
examples: Long story short, our flight was delayed and we missed the connecting train.
synonyms: to make a long story short

word: to cut a long story short
definitions: used to indicate that details are omitted to state a conclusion quickly
examples: To cut a long story short, we managed to resolve issue before midnight.

definitions: used to introduce the most important fact, problem, or explanation in conversation
examples: The thing is, we cannot afford further delays without risking contract cancellation.
synonyms: the fact of the matter is

definitions: used in speech to draw attention to a key point or difficulty
examples: Here is the thing: unless funding arrives soon, construction will stop completely.

definitions: used to state the essential, ultimate, or most important conclusion of discussion
examples: The bottom line is that we must cut expenditure to remain profitable.

definitions: in modern times, in contrast to earlier historical periods
examples: In this day and age, accessing global news instantly has become an expectation for consumers.

definitions: at the present moment; currently under existing circumstances
examples: At this point in time, no official decision has been made regarding executive staff promotions.

definitions: in the present circumstances, as currently situated without further changes
examples: As things stand, the company budget will not support hiring additional full-time software developers.

definitions: for the present moment; temporarily until future developments occur
examples: For the time being, employees are allowed to work remotely three days per week.

definitions: at a critical point where a decisive choice must be made between options
examples: The company found itself at a crossroads when evaluating whether to expand into foreign markets.

definitions: at a moment when a decisive change in a situation occurs, especially with important results
examples: The peace negotiations reached a turning point when both nations signed the bilateral ceasefire agreement.

definitions: an event marking a unique, historic, and irreversible turning point in a situation
examples: The invention of the smartphone represented a watershed moment in global digital personal communication.

definitions: an event, idea, or procedure that significantly changes an existing situation or activity
examples: Developing the high-capacity battery proved to be a game-changer for the electric vehicle industry.

definitions: a fundamental change in approach, underlying assumptions, or basic concepts in a field
examples: The shift toward remote working caused a paradigm shift in modern corporate management strategies.

definitions: clear signs or warnings that a situation is going to fail, end, or deteriorate
examples: When quarterly sales plummeted, employees recognized that the writing was on the wall for store closures.

definitions: the trend, public opinion, or luck is reversing or changing direction noticeably
examples: Analysts observed that the tide is turning in favor of adopting clean renewable energy sources.

definitions: conditions, customs, or societal attitudes are undergoing continuous transformation over time
examples: Traditional retailers realize that times are changing as consumers increasingly prefer convenient online shopping.

definitions: adapting to modern trends, technology, or social changes to remain current and relevant
examples: Legacy financial institutions are investing in mobile applications to ensure keeping up with the times.

definitions: so advanced, innovative, or forward-thinking that it is not appreciated until later
examples: The early electric vehicle model was considered ahead of its time when first introduced decades ago.

definitions: something that is typical or characteristic of the current era or modern social conditions
examples: The closure of traditional bookshops is widely seen as a sad sign of the times.

definitions: something or someone that unexpectedly evokes memories of a previous era or past life
examples: Meeting his childhood best friend at the airport was an unexpected blast from the past.

definitions: past events or disagreements that are forgiven, forgotten, and no longer matter or cause anger
examples: Although they argued bitterly years ago, their past disagreement is now water under the bridge.

definitions: the phenomenon where similar historical events recur in the present owing to unlearned lessons
examples: Fears of history repeating itself emerged when economic inflation rates rose sharply across Europe.
